🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena to Lemus: Free the Water Protesters</u>

Morena demanded the release of the people detained after Jalisco police broke up Sunday's march for clean water at Casa Jalisco. Its message to Movimiento Ciudadano's governor was that repression will never be the way.

The count so far: 39 arrested, 31 civilians needing medical care, and only 18 released. The protest was over Guadalajara's water crisis and fears of privatization.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>China to Mexico: Your Ties With Washington Shouldn't Dictate Who You Trade With</u>

Beijing's special envoy for Latin America, Qiu Xiaoqi (ambassador to Mexico 2013–2019), said China values Mexico–US relations, but they must not affect Mexico's trade with third countries, China included.

He said Mexico has "enough wisdom and experience to handle this properly." The message lands as Mexico's new tariffs on countries without trade agreements hit more than $30 billion in Chinese exports.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Homicides Down 52% in Two Years</u>

Mexico's daily homicide average fell from 86.9 in September 2024 to 42.2 in September 2026, according to the SESNSP. That's 45 fewer murders every single day, and the lowest September since 2015.

All 32 states are down in the first nine months of 2026 vs. 2025. San Luis Potosí leads at −78.6%, then Nayarit at −69.5% and Quintana Roo at −59.7%.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Mexico's Farm Trade Stays in Surplus Despite US Tariffs: $4.28 Billion</u>

Mexico's agri-food trade posted a $4.283 billion surplus from January to August 2026, El Economista reports, down 13.1% from $4.931 billion a year earlier. Exports rose 2.5% to $36.035 billion while imports grew 5.1% to $31.752 billion, as tougher US tariffs hit beer, avocado, berries and sugar, and a stronger peso cut exporters' earnings.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Sheinbaum Tops Latin America's Approval Ranking: 69.3%</u>

CB Global Data's October ranking puts President Sheinbaum first among the leaders of 18 Latin American countries with 69.3% approval, up 0.3 points from September. Behind her: El Salvador's Bukele at 68.3% and the Dominican Republic's Abinader at 51.9%. The survey ran October 5-8.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FGR, SAT and UIF Probe Ex-INE Officials for Embezzlement and Laundering</u>

Federal prosecutors, the tax authority and the Financial Intelligence Unit have opened files on former officials of the INE, Mexico's electoral institute, and five supplier companies over allegedly rigged contracts worth hundreds of millions of pesos, Miguel Badillo reports in Contralínea. Among those under investigation: Jesús Octavio García González, INE's administration chief until April 2026, linked in the case files to altering the 2025 voter-ID card tender to favor Litoformas, a company controlled by his uncle, and Juan Carlos Cuervo Escalona, a coordination director under Lorenzo Córdova. Investigators are also examining whether electoral councillors took part in exchange for kickbacks.

🇲🇽📵 <u>No Phones in Mexican Classrooms: Senate Committees Vote 27-0</u>

The Senate's Education and Legislative Studies committees unanimously approved a General Education Law reform that bars students from using phones in preschool, primary and secondary schools, except for programmed classwork or emergencies. The bill merges 13 initiatives from senators of every party. High schools will set their own limits through consultation. Next stop: the Senate floor, then the Chamber of Deputies.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>Sheinbaum: IMSS Workers' Demands Are Legitimate</u>

After protests across Social Security clinics, President Sheinbaum met IMSS director Zoé Robledo and said the workers' demands are legitimate and must be resolved. She ordered faster regularization of the doctors and nurses hired during COVID who still lack full benefits, and a fix for the distribution failures behind medicine shortages. The raise on the table is now slightly above 5%, up from the 2.9% workers rejected last week.

🇲🇽📊 <u>6.2 Trillion Pesos in Taxes, No Tax Hike</u>

Mexico's 2027 Revenue Law, up for a vote in the Chamber of Deputies this week, projects 6.2 trillion pesos in tax revenue, up 3.9% in real terms. The increase comes from closing deduction and tax-loss abuses by companies earning more than 50 million pesos, not from new taxes. Finance Minister Édgar Amador says tax revenue will reach 15.4% of GDP by the end of 2026: 776 billion pesos more in two years "without the need to raise taxes or carry out a tax reform."
banner: TAXES: +776 BN PESOS, NO NEW TAXES

🇲🇽✊ <u>24.2 Million Mexicans Identify as Indigenous</u>

On the Day of the Pluricultural Nation, INEGI's 2025 intercensal survey counts 24.2 million people, 18.6% of Mexico, who identify as Indigenous; 7.4 million speak an Indigenous language. Indigenous peoples are now recognized in Article 2 of the Constitution as subjects of public law, and the FAISPIAM fund has financed more than 52,000 water, electricity, housing and road projects worth 25 billion pesos. The gap remains: 61% of Indigenous people live in poverty, against 26% of non-Indigenous people.
